summary: The oldest standing lighthouse in the United States, lit in 1764 at the mouth of New York harbour; still showing a third-order Fresnel light, with tours in season.

notes_for_editor: Thin on primary sources: the Lighthouse Board and Commissioner reports in the local corpus cover only 1891-1901 and mostly concern the Hook Beacon and electric-buoy station, not the main tower. Much of the narrative rests on NPS pages (public domain) and Lighthouse Friends (facts only, paraphrased). Disagreements flagged in text: lens 1856/1857; lining 1857/1863; electrification 1894/1896; tower height 103/105 ft and brick/rubblestone; assistants from 1854 (USLHS, LF) or 1857 (NPS); Sarah Patterson Johnson's end date 1882 (USLHS) or 1885 (NPS); Hartshorne owners named Robert and Esek (NPS) vs Esik and Richard (LF), not named in story. The 1933 Bulletin OCR reads 'Handy Hook Point Lio-ht'; read as Sandy Hook Point Light. The 1935 Bulletin storm item is under the heading November Storm Damage (16-18 November); the year 1935 is the volume year, and the Sandy Hook sentence follows the heading by position. Pre-1850s keeper dates differ slightly between USLHS and NPS (e.g. Doane 1819-26 vs 1817-25); the story uses USLHS. A 1924 Bulletin item and the NHL nomination's mention of a lightship 1823 were left out. The Sandy Hook Life-Saving Station (us-nj-sandy-hook-life-saving-station) is a separate record. Tour dates: NPS visit page gives Friday-Monday 1-3:30 p.m.; an NPS event listing (seen only as a search snippet) gives May to August 2026, so tours may be out of season as of 22 October 2026.
